FalsePremTest000.description: Blue/Calculation. 07-24s: needed NO prompt at all, which is why it left the H6 batch. Its engine branch carried TWO paths — an auto-contest when the target's Cognitive defense could be read, and a manual card when it could not. The unreadable-defense case is settled (Ben, §9m q9 / 2bI-8): H1 fails OPEN, project-wide. So the fallback card was the whole reason the talent looked like an H6 consumer, and deleting it leaves clean H1.

HoloSummon000000.description: Blue (Illusion). 2bAA — the whole talent as ONE edha-summon rule (was a name-keyed useItem case). The 1b that unblocked it: `tokenSizeColor` exposes [Size] off your Blue rank, which the engine used to compute in code (edhaSizeFt). `placeAt: pick-point` + `rangeColor: blue` is the CARD's 'within Attunement Range' — the retired case placed the illusion beside you and checked no range at all (card-is-spec, §9m q11); a cancelled or out-of-range click REFUNDS the Investiture. BarricadeH220000.description: Blue (Illusion). 2bAA — H22 `edha-barrier`, the engine's FIRST blocks-movement capability, built because the card demanded three things the engine delivered none of: placement AT A POINT in Attunement Range, blocking movement, and cover. What shipped was a one-square token spawned beside you that anyone could walk through. Now: click-place within Blue Attunement Range (cancel, out of range, or an occupied square REFUNDS the Investiture — a closed wall box around a creature would trap it), an HP token rolled at 2[Die] on the Blue track, and a box of four real Foundry walls around its square. blocksSight stays `none` because a shimmering illusion is seen through and COVER IS A TABLE READ project-wide — flip the field if a barrier should block line of sight. It comes down when destroyed, when its token is deleted, or at the end of the encounter. Sustain-multiple (Ben 06-14e): no cap. The picker, the wall documents and their GM relay stay ENGINE-OWNED, keyed on this rule (§9o).

handler.note: It also provides cover to anything behind it — how much is the table's call, as every cover read in this system is.

ReactAnalMod0000.description: Blue/Foresight. 07-24r: it reads in the audit as an H8 watcher and it is not one. The trigger ('a character in range fails a test') is the REACTION's trigger — volition, which no hook owns — and the mechanic is the on-use grant the engine already had. So it needed no handler at all, only `edha-next-test-mod` on `use`. `bindToTarget` is new and makes the talent match its own text: the advantage is spent on a test AGAINST the creature you have targeted, not on any test at all (2bI-2). Nothing targeted → it stays unbound rather than failing.

handler.text: advantage on your next test against the creature that just failed — target it when you use this and the advantage binds to it.
